**Answer each of the following questions with *one sentence* including a brief explanation.**

1.  Finish the sentence with another student’s name: "If \[Name of Student\] doesn’t earn an A, then nobody should, because..." Explain your choice and your reasoning.

    If [Lucy]{.underline} doesn't earn an A, then nobody should, because she consistently contributes to class discussions, asks questions on Discord, and demonstrates deep understanding in her assignments.

2.  What was the most difficult part of the class for you? List a general topic, a specific problem, a kind of work we did, etc. and explain why.

    Using the {{ }} operator in data frame functions was most difficult because understanding when and how to properly use this advanced tidy evaluation syntax required significant practice and debugging. It took me a bit to understand data frames.

3.  What was the easiest part of the class for you? Explain why.

    Creating visualizations with ggplot2 was easiest because the grammar of graphics provides an intuitive, consistent framework that builds logically from data to plot elements.

4.  What part of the class surprised or interested you the most? Explain why.

    The power and flexibility of ggplot2 surprised me most, as I discovered how even simple adjustments to aesthetics and themes could transform basic plots into professional, publication-ready visualizations.

5.  Give one piece of advice to a student just beginning a quarter of STAT 331 that will help them be successful in learning.

    Start practicing proper citation habits from day one and thoroughly complete every revision, as these skills build both technical proficiency and professional credibility throughout the course.
